clue.text: Special occasion —. going into it, he's ordered platinum to celebrate

indicators.note: going into tells us the event is placed inside the jumbled letters that follow
ordered means put into a new order, so the letters of it and he's are rearranged

parts.note: taken as written, the letters H, E and S
an event is a special occasion

explanation.surface: Someone marking a big occasion orders platinum to celebrate it.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes 'Special occasion' look like the definition; it is the inserted piece, and 'ordered' gives SIETH. Platinum marks a seventy-year anniversary.
explanation.definitionFit: A platinum anniversary or jubilee marks seventy years, so platinum is the gift for that milestone.

clue.text: Not so quick to catch a pair of fellows making a bloomer

indicators.note: to catch means to hold inside, so the word for not so quick takes in the other letters

parts.note: slower means not so quick
F is fellow, so two of them give FF

explanation.surface: A slow runner traps two blokes, making an embarrassing error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bloomer' looks like a blunder; it is a flowering plant.
explanation.definitionFit: Safflower is a thistle-like plant grown for its flowers and oil, so something that blooms.

clue.text: Rather green doctor possesses right level of proficiency

indicators.note: possesses means holds, so the doctor holds the other letters inside

parts.note: a vet is an animal doctor
a dan is a grade of skill in judo and karate

explanation.surface: An inexperienced doctor has reached the proper standard of competence.
explanation.definitionFit: Verdant means fresh and green, and by extension naive and inexperienced.

clue.text: Factor in experimental procedure led to ordeal on the underground

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above, so the ordeal comes before the underground

parts.note: a test is a trial or ordeal
the Tube is London's underground railway

explanation.surface: An experiment's variables led to a trying journey on the London Underground.
explanation.definitionFit: A glass tube for samples is a standard item in a laboratory experiment.

clue.text: As a real clue cost will vary, see this item in contract

indicators.note: will vary means will change, so these letters are changed into another order

explanation.surface: Since a genuine clue's price will fluctuate, check the relevant term in the agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'will vary' rearranges AS A REAL CLUE COST; 'see this' links to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A provision in a contract allowing prices or wages to rise in step with costs.

clue.text: Well, one should be in 'this, if it's good

definitions.text: Well, one should be in 'this, if it's good

parts.words: Well, one should be in 'this, if it's good
parts.note: being well means being in a good state of bodily fitness

explanation.surface: A remark that you ought to be in some place if it is a decent one.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone well is in good condition physically, the state of their body.

clue.text: Handle height by going backwards?

parts.note: aft means towards the back of a ship, so heading backwards

explanation.surface: A question about a handle that shrinks as it slides backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A haft is the handle of a knife, axe or tool.

clue.text: Apology for consumers?

parts.note: an apology described as food: to say sorry humbly is idiomatically to eat a dish of this

explanation.surface: A company saying sorry to its customers.
explanation.definitionFit: To eat this dish is an idiom for making a humiliating apology.

clue.text: One's imagined battle with chaps turning out hard —-

indicators.note: with here means holding inside, so the chaps go within the trimmed word
hard is H, and turning it out removes that letter

parts.note: a fight is a battle
men are chaps

explanation.surface: A battle with men that turned out to be imagined.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hard' looks like a description of the battle, but it is just the letter H, leaving FIGT once removed.
explanation.definitionFit: A figment is a thing invented by the mind, something made up.

clue.text: In favour, since revamp of legal practice

parts.note: for means in favour of, as in 'for or against'

indicators.note: a revamp remodels something, so the letters of since are rebuilt in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone backs reforming the law since it badly needs a revamp.
explanation.walkthrough: 'legal practice' tempts as the definition, but 'practice' is part of the adjectival phrase; 'revamp' yields ENSIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Forensic describes things used in courts of law, as in forensic evidence.

clue.text: Some charm a ghillie displayed, in the county

indicators.note: Some signals that only part of the following words is taken, a run lying across them

explanation.surface: A Scottish gamekeeper shows some charm out in the countryside.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across charM A GHillie. A ghillie is a Scottish hunting or fishing guide.
explanation.definitionFit: Armagh is one of the six counties of Northern Ireland.

clue.text: See page put together to disclose secrets

explanation.surface: Advice to glance at a page and assemble the facts before revealing confidential matters.
explanation.walkthrough: The first half is indirect: SEE plus P (page) put together makes SEEP, and to seep is to escape through a gap, the same as the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses share the word: liquid seeping out escapes through a crack, and someone revealing secrets lets information slip out.

clue.text: My relations are sometimes malicious

parts.note: relations here are not family but stories told; the speaker is a gossip whose accounts can be spiteful

explanation.surface: Someone admits their relatives can be spiteful.
explanation.definitionFit: A gossip who spreads stories, the relations here, often does so out of malice.

clue.text: Collector waiting to receive what's not exactly out of the blue!

definitions.text: Collector waiting to receive what's not exactly out of the blue!

parts.words: Collector waiting to receive what's not exactly out of the blue!
parts.note: the collector is a garden container waiting for rain, which falls from grey clouds rather than a blue sky

explanation.surface: A collector waiting for something that does not come entirely unexpectedly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the blue' usually means unexpectedly; here it is the sky, and rain rarely comes from a clear blue one.
explanation.definitionFit: A large barrel set under a downpipe collects rainwater for the garden.

clue.text: — used to have an advantage

parts.note: describes someone or something used unfairly so that another gains from it

explanation.surface: Something was used to gain an edge.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash links it to the end of 7 Down, so it reads on from that clue.
explanation.definitionFit: To exploit a person or resource is to use them for profit or gain.

clue.text: Suddenly got a lot of stick, making son leader?

indicators.note: son is S, and making it the leader moves that letter to the front of the word

parts.note: paste is stuff that makes things stick, a glue

explanation.surface: Someone suddenly got a lot of criticism after promoting their son to head the firm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stick' looks like criticism in the surface but is glue.
explanation.definitionFit: A spate is a sudden rush or flood of something, a lot arriving at once.

clue.text: In all seriousness, sooner set about cosy home-making

indicators.note: set about means placed around, so the word for sooner goes around the cosy home

parts.note: early means sooner than expected
a nest is a snug home

explanation.surface: Seriously, the sooner you start making a snug home the better.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something earnestly means doing it with sincere, serious intent.

clue.text: Not likely to include circular-type letter

parts.note: O is a circular shape
a missive is a letter

explanation.surface: A circular letter is unlikely to contain everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Omissive means tending to leave things out, the opposite of inclusive.

clue.text: A record kept by right-hand man

indicators.note: kept by means held inside, so A and the record sit within the outer pair

parts.note: R is right and H is hand, two abbreviations together
an LP is a long-playing record

explanation.surface: A record kept by an assistant, someone's right-hand man.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph is a man's name; crosswords often define a first name simply as man.

clue.text: Losing voice, and drunk, hop in, given lift by ex-drinkers

indicators.note: being given a lift means carried inside a vehicle, so the jumble sits within the ex-drinkers

parts.note: AA is Alcoholics Anonymous, people who have given up drink

indicators.note: drunk means tipsy and disordered, so the letters of hop in are shuffled

explanation.surface: A drunk who has lost their voice hops into a car offered by recovering alcoholics.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunk' looks like a description of the person but is the anagram signal, giving PHONI; the ex-drinkers are Alcoholics Anonymous.
explanation.definitionFit: Aphonia is the medical term for the inability to speak, loss of the voice.

clue.text: One touting own skills perhaps, doing a Jumbo?

definitions.text: One touting own skills perhaps, doing a Jumbo?

parts.words: One touting own skills perhaps, doing a Jumbo?
parts.note: a braggart blows their own horn, and Jumbo the elephant raises its trunk and makes the same loud call

explanation.surface: A show-off behaves like a big elephant.
explanation.definitionFit: A boaster is said to blow their own horn, and elephants make a brassy call like a brass player.

clue.text: Nicholas's wife under a terrible strain? No, getting over it

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting over means placed above, so the jumble comes before the A
terrible means awful and in a mess, so the letters of strain are jumbled

explanation.surface: The last Tsar's wife was under terrible strain but got over it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'terrible' rearranges STRAIN into TSARIN. 'under a' would put the A first; 'No' cancels that, and the jumble goes over the A instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Tsar Nicholas II's wife Alexandra was the Russian empress, the title of a tsar's consort.

clue.text: Hunter's aide given another spell employed in 9 Across?

definitions.text: Hunter's aide given another spell employed in 9 Across?

parts.words: Hunter's aide given another spell employed in 9 Across?
parts.note: the gamekeeper word in the clue to 9 Across, written there with an H, spelt another way

explanation.surface: A hunting assistant takes another turn of duty in the county.
explanation.walkthrough: The 9 Across clue contains 'ghillie'; 'another spell' means the alternative spelling without the H, not another work shift.
explanation.definitionFit: A gillie is a Scottish attendant on a hunting or fishing trip.

clue.text: Book events listed by The Times

explanation.surface: A book of news events catalogued by a famous newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: One is the Old Testament books of that name; the other is the verb for recording events in order, as a newspaper does.

clue.text: The Red Sea?

parts.note: read as a red pigment that is also a body of water smaller than a sea, rather than the famous gulf

explanation.surface: A question about the stretch of water between Africa and Arabia.
explanation.walkthrough: Lake is a crimson pigment as well as an inland stretch of water, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: The word names both a deep red dye and an inland body of water, a sort of small sea.

clue.text: This month, being poorly, finally neglected to drop in

parts.note: inst., short for instant, means this month in old business letters

indicators.note: the final letter is neglected, so the last letter of the word for poorly is dropped

parts.note: ill means poorly or unwell

explanation.surface: Someone who was ill this month forgot, in the end, to call round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'finally neglected' drops the last L of ILL to leave IL.
explanation.definitionFit: To instil is to introduce something gradually, as drops of liquid are added one at a time.

clue.text: As a left-winger, do I favour joint enterprise?

definitions.text: As a left-winger, do I favour joint enterprise?

parts.words: As a left-winger, do I favour joint enterprise?
parts.note: a member of a trade organisation, typically on the left, supports workers joining together

explanation.surface: A socialist asks whether they back cooperative ventures.
explanation.definitionFit: A trade union member supports collective action, workers joined together in one body.

clue.text: Go on the attack, getting a clear round

indicators.note: round means surrounding, so the word for clear goes around the A

parts.note: to rid is to clear of something

explanation.surface: Attacking after getting a clean round in a contest.
explanation.definitionFit: A raid is a sudden attack, and to raid is to make one.

clue.text: Simple description of subatomic particle

explanation.surface: A plain account of a tiny piece of matter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means basic; an elementary particle in physics has no smaller parts.
